title: Split runner protocol and introduce lightweight iterator to decouple loadgen from orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The current eval/load harness tightly couples the scenario runner, adapter layer, and orchestration loop. This makes small changes expensive (high churn), causes large memory spikes for long sequences, and prevents us from reliably reproducing perf regressions across CI and local runs. It also depends on an older queueing library (legacy-queue v1.9) that complicates async upgrades and backpressure reasoning.

Goal: Break the runner into a small protocol boundary + a lightweight, pull-based iterator abstraction so: 1) load generators (synthetic or recorded) can be consumed by both the CI orchestration and ad-hoc local tooling without duplicating logic; 2) we reduce memory allocation spikes for long sequences by streaming inputs and outputs; 3) deterministic seeding can be enforced at the iterator boundary; 4) remove legacy-queue dependency and migrate to the async-stream primitives used across the infra.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Define RunnerProtocol interface and Iterator abstraction (pull-based with optional prefetch window).
- Implement adapter wrappers for existing load adapters (gpt-load, replay-corpus, microbench) to conform to Iterator.
- Replace legacy-queue dependency with async-streams and a small backpressure shim used by the orchestrator.
- Add deterministic seeding support (seed metadata carried with iterator items and a deterministic RNG implementation used in CI).
- Update perf-regression CI job to exercise both the new iterator and the old runner in a migration A/B mode for 2 cycles.
- Provide a compatibility shim for third-party internal consumers for one release cycle.

Out of scope: deep rewrites of orchestration scheduling policies, KV cache algorithms, and model runner internals. Those will be follow-ups once the boundary is stable.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Regression harness memory usage for long-sequence scenario reduced by >= 35% on p3.xlarge test VM.
- Reproducibility: same token-level latency distribution for local and CI runs (statistical similarity p>0.95) when using the deterministic seed.
- CI perf-regression runs complete without flakiness increase (no >1.5x increase in CI time).
- Legacy-queue package removed from test infra and runtime-dev images.

Rollout plan: implement the RunnerProtocol and Iterator, ship adapters behind a feature-flag, run two full perf-regression cycles in A/B mode (old runner vs new iterator). If metrics meet success criteria, flip flag and remove compatibility shim after one release.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle ordering differences for stateful adapters (replay-corpus with user-defined pauses). Mitigation: add an ordering-preservation test harness and a tape-mode run to validate behavior early.
- Risk: third-party CI scripts rely on internal queue semantics. Mitigation: compatibility shim + deprecation notices in internal docs and Slack channel.
- Risk: transient perf regressions from async-stream overhead. Mitigation: microbench the shim and iterators; inline hot paths after measurement.

Implementation notes: prefer zero-copy buffers for payloads, use the platform RNG wrapper (rng/v2) for deterministic seeding, and keep the new iterator as a minimal trait to avoid heavy runtime reflection. Document API in /confluence/eval-harness/runner-protocol.md.
